title: MCP Apps — Interactive UI Resources via `ui://`

questions.question: What UI resource does tool_visualize_timeline return for the notes timeline?
questions.explanation: The tool result points at the exact MCP App resource URI ui://notes/timeline.

questions.question: Which MIME type does resources_read use for the timeline UI?
questions.explanation: The exact UI resource is served as text/html with the mcp-app profile so the host treats it as an interactive MCP App.

questions.question: Which security properties are present in the timeline tool result?
options: A wildcard connect-src and filesystem permission
An OAuth token embedded in the HTML
No CSP because SVG is automatically safe
questions.explanation: The result carries the explicit TIMELINE_CSP policy and permissions is [], rather than granting extra host capabilities.

questions.question: How does the generated page communicate its initial UI request?
options: It posts JSON-RPC messages with postMessage, including ui/initialize
It calls an HTTP endpoint on notes.example.com
It waits for a CLI prompt
questions.explanation: The self-contained HTML uses window messaging and sends a JSON-RPC ui/initialize message to the host.

questions.question: What does resources_read do for a URI other than ui://notes/timeline?
options: It returns the timeline for every URI
It aliases all notes:// URIs to the app
It creates a new app resource
questions.explanation: The demo exposes one exact UI URI; an unknown URI is rejected with ValueError rather than silently substituted.

questions.question: Which host entrypoints are demonstrated by the app HTML?
options: OAuth authorize, token, and revoke only
tools/list and tools/call without a host object
questions.explanation: The printed host bridge includes callTool, readResource, getPrompt, and close so the UI can request host-mediated capabilities.
